From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-18T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Observability hooks and SDK integration - post-demo follow-up

Hi Alex - thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

1) Integration surface: you confirmed the primary flows will be (a) real-time chat completions via SDK, (b) nightly batch embeddings for search, and (c) a reranking pipeline for top-k candidates.

2) Auth & SDK: you asked about supported auth flows. Redwood supports API keys (short-term tokens), OAuth for service accounts, and mutual TLS for Private deployments. For the SDK we can provide a short snippet for your Node and Python services - attaching auth/snippets.

3) Routing & model variants: recommended pattern is to use route tags (e.g., route=low-latency vs route=cost-optimized) in the request metadata so your gateway can pick the right backend. We'll share a sample middleware for request routing.

4) Observability hooks (your main ask): we propose the following minimal headers/fields to instrument across your stack:
   - X-Redwood-Trace-Id: a UUID per user interaction (propagate downstream)
   - X-Redwood-Request-Id: unique per API call for token-level breakdowns
   - X-Redwood-Routing: route tag used (low-latency | cost | cached)
   - X-Redwood-Model-Variant: model id + quantization profile
   - Response headers: X-Redwood-Server-Latency (ms), X-Redwood-Queue-Time (ms)

We'll also emit structured JSON logs (fields: trace_id, request_id, route, model_variant, stage_latency) that map to your Splunk/CloudWatch fields.

Action items from Redwood:
- I'll attach the observability guide and SDK auth snippets (done).
- Marcus to share short middleware snippet for routing + header propagation.
- Marissa to share a mutual action plan and target dates (attachment).

Can you confirm that the trace/request header names above work for you and that you have capacity to add X-Redwood-Trace-Id propagation on the frontend/mobile SDK? We can provide a 2-hour pairing session for the initial rollout.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_observability_guide.pdf, sdk-auth-snippets.zip, mutual-action-plan.xlsx

Thanks Marissa - this is helpful. A few clarifying questions from our engineering team: 

1) For X-Redwood-Trace-Id, do you require 128-bit UUIDs or is any unique string ok? We're using AWS X-Ray trace IDs today and would prefer to map instead of re-generating if possible.

2) For the token-level latency breakdowns, what's the recommended way to correlate per-token timing when we stream responses? Is the X-Redwood-Request-Id sufficient, or do you recommend adding chunk-level ids?

3) For embeddings/rerank: our batch job runs in GKE and uses service accounts. We'll need a sample for short-lived OAuth tokens (15m) - can you confirm the OAuth flow and refresh window?

We'd like the Node SDK snippet; could Marcus drop the middleware into the thread so our infra person can test quickly? Also please share any dashboard templates so we can mirror the same dashboards on our side.

Alex
Sr. Engineering Manager, Integrations
FinTechCo
